verdict.rationale: Ubuntu's own site explicitly claims that, as a lightweight and efficient OS, installing it on older hardware can improve performance and extend device lifespan. That claim is only a marketing statement, with no supporting specifics. One community user cites bloat and preferred another distro for performance, but that report is not about older hardware, so it lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: documented minimum or older-hardware system requirements, benchmarks or guidance for older machines, independent or hands-on corroboration of performance gains on aging devices.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can get better performance and extended device lifespan by installing the OS on older hardware

citations.quote: As a lightweight and highly efficient operating system, installing Ubuntu on older hardware can improve performance and extend the lifespan of your devices.
